  \item \textbf{Domain dependence of $\Kempirical$}: general web text (C4, Wikipedia) and code yield $\Kempirical{\leq}2$, while structured academic text (arXiv) yields $\Kempirical{=}3$, consistent across model families (Section~\ref{sec:cross_domain}).
  \item \textbf{Generator-agnostic cross-model transfer} (within continuation mode): 15 statistical features enable 80--92\% accuracy retention with scorer-invariant feature rankings ($\rho > 0.90$), supporting depth estimation on corpora from unknown continuation-mode generators without retraining; $\Kempirical$ agreement holds across scorers for strong-signal configurations (Section~\ref{sec:transfer}).

\paragraph{Model collapse and recursive degradation.}
Iterative training on model outputs causes tail-distribution degradation~\cite{shumailov2024collapse, alemohammad2024selfconsuming, dohmatob2024model, dohmatob2025strong, fu2025theoretical}, diversity contraction~\cite{guo2024curious, padmakumar2024writing, briesch2023selfconsuming}, and predictable convergence~\cite{schaeffer2025position, kazdan2025collapse, gerstgrasser2024model, wang2025unveiling}.
Our prompt-chain operates in the replace regime~\cite{kazdan2025collapse}, making $\Kempirical = 2$ a conservative lower bound.
Markov chain convergence theory predicts that recursive generation converges to a stationary distribution~\cite{fu2025theoretical}, complementing the DPI's mutual information monotonicity; empirically, detection accuracy erodes with each generation~\cite{hao2025rewrite}, consistent with our measured discrimination boundary.
This literature characterizes macro dynamics but provides no per-text depth estimation, the gap we address.

\paragraph{Beyond binary detection.}
Binary detectors~\cite{mitchell2023detectgpt, bao2024fast, hans2024binoculars, basani2026diveye, zhang2024minkpp} achieve strong human-vs.-machine separation but produce no depth estimate; other systems such as Ghostbuster~\cite{verma2024ghostbuster} and GPTZero~\cite{liang2023gpt}, as well as benchmarks like RAID~\cite{dugan2024raid}, likewise target the binary task without estimating generational depth.
Recent work extends beyond binary labels to collaboration degree~\cite{cheng2025beyond}, contamination hierarchies~\cite{mehta2025beyond}, and multigenerator benchmarks~\cite{wang2024semeval}; robustness concerns arise under paraphrasing~\cite{sadasivan2023detect, krishna2023paraphrasing} and cross-mode transfer~\cite{hao2025rewrite}; CoDeC~\cite{zawalski2026codec} addresses contamination via membership inference.
None estimates recursive generation depth.

\paragraph{Data curation, ordinal methods, and watermarking.}
Data Selection with Importance Resampling (DSIR)~\cite{xie2023dsir}, D4~\cite{tirumala2023d4}, and DoReMi~\cite{xie2023doremi} are depth-agnostic; Drayson et al.~\cite{drayson2025} combined binary detection with importance resampling, a special case when $\Kstar = 1$.
Our OBD classifier follows Frank \& Hall's~\cite{frank2001ordinal} binary decomposition; our neural probe extends probing~\cite{alain2017understanding, belinkov2022probing} to the discrimination boundary.
Text watermarking~\cite{kirchenbauer2023watermark} embeds provenance signals proactively; our work addresses the complementary post-hoc scenario where the generator is not controlled.

tool_args.new_string:
We introduced the discrimination boundary $\Kempirical$, the maximum generational depth at which adjacent generations remain statistically distinguishable, and measured it across 10 prompt-chain configurations spanning six architecture families at 1B--8B scale.
The central finding is that $\Kempirical \leq 2$ universally for web text (C4, Wikipedia, code): beyond two generation passes, recursive synthetic text becomes indistinguishable from shallower synthetic text under both supervised (OBD) and zero-shot (frontier LLM) classifiers.
Structured academic text (arXiv) reaches $\Kempirical{=}3$ across four independent architecture families, driven by larger per-generation distributional shift; the domain dependence of $\Kempirical$ implies that the discrimination boundary is a text-intrinsic property rather than a model artifact.

The one-wash laundering effect concentrates the exploitable signal at the human-vs.-machine boundary (0v1), with 1v2 AUC dropping by ${\sim}$30\,pp and deeper pairs falling below chance-corrected thresholds.
This has direct practical implications: binary curation halves the MMLU degradation gap under extreme contamination, while graduated strategies that rely on depth estimates beyond $\Kempirical$ inject noise from near-random classifier outputs and offer no benefit.
At realistic contamination ratios ($\leq$50\%), all strategies converge, confirming that depth-aware filtering matters most when contamination is severe.

Generator-agnostic statistical features enable cross-model transfer at 80--92\% accuracy retention, with scorer-invariant feature rankings ($\rho > 0.90$), supporting depth estimation on corpora from unknown continuation-mode generators without retraining.
The cost of generator-agnostic features is bounded: neural probes extend $\Kempirical$ by one depth level, and a DeBERTa upper-bound probe reaches $\Kempirical{=}4$ on arXiv, suggesting that richer representations can push the boundary further at the expense of generator specificity.

Several directions remain open: extending depth-chain generation beyond 8B scale to frontier models, evaluating RLHF/DPO-aligned models where post-training alignment may alter the degradation profile, and closing the gap between the empirically measured $\Kempirical$ and the theoretical bound $\Ktheory$ implied by the Data Processing Inequality.

Several directions remain open: depth chains beyond 8B scale, RLHF/DPO-aligned models where post-training alignment may alter degradation, and closing the $\Kempirical$--$\Ktheory$ gap.
